display_name: Penal Code 1871 — seven property and intimidation offences, s 301, and the form of a charge
versions_encoded: Penal Code 1871 as in force 17 September 2026 (2020 Revised Edition with amendments to Act 21 of 2025)
s 301 as substituted by Act 15 of 2019, in force 1 January 2020
scope: Sections 22–25 (property, wrongful gain and loss, dishonestly, fraudulently); 378–379 theft and 380 theft in dwelling; 383–384 extortion; 390, 392, 393, 394 robbery; 403 dishonest misappropriation of property; 405–409 criminal breach of trust (s 405 defines it; s 406 punishes it; ss 407, 408 and 409 punish it in an aggravated capacity, each built on the s 405 node); 415, 417, 420 cheating; 503, 506 criminal intimidation; 321, 323A hurt; 301 transferred malice. s 403 both defines and punishes, so it exports two things rather than three: the ladder IS the defining section. Each punishing section exports a charge builder that recites the charge in the form the Criminal Procedure Code 2010 ss 123–126 prescribe, or refuses with the elements not made out (CPC s 123(5)). Riders: s 34 common intention as a header clause only; no s 404 (misappropriation of property possessed by a deceased person), no s 109 abetment, no CPC s 124(4) amalgamation, no general attempt under s 511 (s 393, which punishes an attempt at robbery specifically, IS encoded); of the theft family's five punishing sections only ss 379 and 380 are encoded — ss 379A, 381 and 382 are not, and NOTES.md lists them with their punishments. Illustrations and Explanations are carried as comments and as @desc text, not as rules. The evidence layer (what a fact rests on) is app-side, not encoded.
